summary.headline: IDFC First Bank Q1 FY27 profit crossed INR1,000 crores for the first time at INR1,075 crores, up about 132% YoY, with GNPA at 1.51%.
summary.overview: Profit rose to INR1,075 crores, helped by NII growth of 21.1% YoY and lower provisions of INR1,144 crores after a INR514.8 crore CGFMU claim receipt. Asset quality improved on GNPA (1.51%, down 10 bps QoQ) and NNPA (0.44%), and the bank made a voluntary contingency provision of INR515 crores. Management raised its full-year ROA ambition to about 1% and cut its FY27 credit cost guidance to 150-160 bps from 170-180 bps. NIM was 5.96% reported, but management said it would settle near 5.8% for the year.

financial_highlights.change: +3 bps QoQ from 5.93%; adjusted ~5.85% to 5.90% ex day-count and IT refund benefits
+16.4% YoY; +2.3% QoQ excluding Q4 fraud one-off
-31.1% YoY from INR1,659 crores; flat QoQ
CET1 hit ~30 bps from ops risk RWA reset
+19% YoY; 4.8 million cards in force; spends +22% YoY

segments.name: Retail, agri and MSME
segments.commentary: Book at INR2.4 lakh crores, growing about 18% YoY; GNPA 1.40% (down 7 bps QoQ) and NNPA 0.52% (down 4 bps QoQ).

segments.name: Wholesale
segments.commentary: Book at INR64,000 crores, growing about 30% YoY, faster than retail; management said corporate NIM is somewhat lower than retail.

segments.name: Microfinance
segments.commentary: Book at INR6,700 crores, marginally up QoQ; 93% covered under CGFMU; SMA 1+2 normalised to 0.71%; FY27 book growth target about 15% YoY.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: CASA crossed INR1.58 lakh crores, up about 8% QoQ; NRI deposits about INR25,000 crores, about 1.7% of the INR1.65 trillion system pool.

guidance_outlook: NIM for FY27 now seen around 5.8%, versus earlier 5.75% guidance; cost of funds to stay near 6%; no rate hike assumed.
Credit cost for FY27 now seen at 150-160 bps, versus earlier 170-180 bps.
Full-year FY27 ROA targeted at about 1%, with management hoping to sustain or exceed it; Q1 ROA was about 0.9% (about 0.9% adjusted for treasury gain, per management).
Opex growth guided at 13-14% for the year; the 450-500 bps positive jaw is to be maintained at minimum.
Cost to income targeted below 70% during the year from 70.7% in Q1.
Management said ROA could structurally reach 1.7-1.8% over time, without a specific date.
ECL transition capital impact expected to be broadly neutral; run-rate impact described as manageable, with no number given yet.
FCNR(B) target share of about 2.5% of an assumed USD 60-70 billion inflow; FCNR rate announced at 6.75%.
capex_capacity: Management highlighted a modernised technology stack (cloud, API-first, event-driven, microservices, real-time data streaming); IT expense share of opex has fallen to about 9% from about 11%.
Insourcing of channel sourcing is being built product by product; channel sourcing expense is about 20% of opex and expected to grow broadly with volumes.
Ops risk RWA reset caused about 30 bps CET1 impact in Q1 and is typical each Q1.
PSL holdings about INR1.2 lakh crores; the bank remains a net buyer of PSLCs and lost about INR250 crores on PSLC purchases last year.
demand_pricing: Disbursements rose about 25%+ YoY in Q1, supporting fee income growth of 22.9% YoY.
Total income rose 21.5% YoY, versus 17.1% reported for the previous quarter.
MFI disbursements almost doubled YoY, but book growth remains muted.
Average CA deposits up about 30% YoY and SA up about 25%; management said SA growth was granular.
Management said deposit inflows are strong and institutional deposits are stable after the earlier episode; the bank plans to tilt toward retail deposits over time.

qa_highlights.question: Will the asset mix shift compress margins toward 5.75% for the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said full-year NIM could be around 5.8%, up from the earlier 5.75% guide. Cost of funds should stay near 6%, but growth in NIM-dilutive segments and normalising investment book could weigh; no rate hike assumed.

qa_highlights.question: Can credit cost guidance be cut after Q1 at 153 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY27 credit cost is now seen at 150-160 bps versus 170-180 bps earlier. He added that the Q1 contingency provision of INR515 crores is prudent and covers later-year geopolitical and monsoon risks.

qa_highlights.question: How will ECL transition affect capital and run-rate credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said transition capital impact is broadly neutral, with higher ECL provisions offset by RWA relief. Run-rate effect is expected to be manageable, helped by EIR amortisation of fees and sourcing costs; no number was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FCNR opportunity and mobilisation so far?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said NRI deposits are about INR25,000 crores, about 1.7% of the system. He targets about 2.5% of an assumed USD 60-70 billion inflow via leverage and SBLC structure; mobilisation is just starting and no figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 ROA of around 1% still on track, and what is the path for FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said full-year FY27 ROA of about 1% is the aim. For FY28, the CEO said the cost-to-income gap of about 350 bps should carry forward if the 450-500 bps positive jaw repeats, and that ROA should rise naturally.

qa_highlights.question: Have there been any recoveries from the fraud incident?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said recovery is in a legal and PMLA court process, with no timeline. No recovery has been booked in Q1.

risks_watch: Margin compression from asset mix shift and a lower investment book; Q1 NIM benefited from about 6 bps IT refund interest and 8 bps day-count in Q4.
Macro risks cited by management: geopolitical tensions (Middle East war), monsoon, and the new ECL regime's run-rate provisioning impact.
Opex growth could rise if business momentum continues; management tied the 500 bps jaw to income growth of about 18.5-20.5%.
Uncertain timing and size of fraud-related recoveries, which are not in Q1 P&L.
CGFMU claims are annual, so the INR514.8 crore receipt is unlikely to repeat in full in FY28.
Corporate-book growth may dilute NIM; management said the mix shift is expected to continue.
Uncertain FCNR inflows and their rate cost.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on earnings momentum, asset quality and deposits, with specific upgrades to ROA, NIM and credit-cost guidance. Management was more cautious on macro risks, and on the timing and size of fraud recoveries. The CEO's remarks on governance and customer-first culture were more qualitative and less tied to numbers.

growth.why: Guidance is mostly on margins, credit cost and ROA (ROA ~1%, opex growth 13-14%, cost-to-income below 70%) rather than volume growth; the only explicit growth targets are MFI book +15% YoY and FCNR share ~2.5%, backed by disbursement momentum (+25% YoY) and a 21.5% total income rise, with no capacity additions disclosed.
